name: Hendre Forest
blurb: Nine hundred acres of Sitka spruce in rows so straight you could use them to check a ruler. Under the needles, the ground is the colour of an old biscuit and the wildlife has been politely absent since the 1960s.
ranger: Welcome to your forest. Don't be alarmed by the silence. That's the spruce, it drinks all the light and shares none of it.
We've felled the first coupe and left the stumps for the beetles. Looks like a battlefield, I know. Give it a season and it will start to look like a plan.
Oak and birch coming up through the brash, and a kite hanging about over the ride. There's a light on in this wood that wasn't here in spring.
A pine marten, last week, at the top ride. It sat there like it was reading the planning permission. The Forestry would be proud, and slightly baffled.
